label: first two copy-phase inputs (and last two) in long sequences
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, and only on repeated tokens (never on original-phase or delimiter steps). Most activation mass (~69%) is on the first two copy steps (inputs orig(0) and orig(1), recall_idx 1-2), and it is strongly concentrated in long sequences (L=9 holds 65% of mass, L=8 23%, almost nothing for L<=5). A second, smaller mode is the last two copy steps of L=9 sequences (t=16,17). Within these positions, magnitude depends on the input token: e, s, h, r, z, w, x, l, b give the largest activations (the top examples are all at recall_idx 1-2 with inputs like e/s/w/r), and restricting to those tokens raises precision to ~0.73 at the cost of recall. Precision of the position-only predicate is ~0.40, so token identity and length together set whether it crosses threshold; mid-copy steps carry low, scattered activation.
